sentences.text:
The respondent No.2 lodged the FIR alleging that the petitioner No.1 - husband and the petitioners No.2 and 3 - parents-in-law and others accused subjected her to cruelty NC:
2023:KHC:41224 both mentally and physically and also a demand was made to bring money from the parental home.

The police registered the FIR for the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of D P Act.
4.

The parties are present before this Court and have filed a memorandum of compromise petition stating that the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.2 - defacto complainant had filed a petition in MC No.6711/2023 under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolving their marriage mutually and in terms of the settlement, their marriage has been dissolved mutually and the respondent No.2 has agreed to withdraw all the allegations against the petitioners herein and further a sum of Rs.2,00,00,000/- is paid to the respondent No.2 towards permanent alimony.
5. The memorandum of compromise petition is placed on record.

6. Though the offences are cognizable and non- compoundable, however, having regard to the fact that, the parties have amicably settled the dispute among themselves, and the respondent No.2 having agreed to withdraw all the allegations made by her, it would be futile exercise if the petitioners - accused are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
NC: 2023:KHC:41224 ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned FIR in Crime No.0275/2023 registered by the Amruthahalli Police Station, Bangalore, is hereby quashed.
